groups.name: dataset
groups.purpose: The generated events are reproducible and internally consistent.

checks.claim: Rebuilding the dataset with the same seed reproduces it byte for byte.
checks.detail: Two independent generator runs in this process were hashed and compared.

checks.claim: Every event points at a user and an item that exist in the catalog.
A learner never interacts with the same item twice.
checks.detail: The simulator draws without replacement. Real logs repeat, so repeat-exposure handling is untested by this dataset.

checks.claim: The event log is stored in chronological order.
All four implicit actions occur often enough to be learnable.
Every learner contributes the same number of events.
checks.detail: Uniform activity is a simulator artifact. Real traffic is heavy-tailed, so this dataset cannot exercise sparse-user behaviour.

groups.name: split
groups.purpose: The three time windows are disjoint, ordered, and free of item leakage.

checks.claim: The three windows partition the event log with no overlap and no loss.
For every learner, history precedes ranker fit, which precedes evaluation.
checks.detail: This is the check that would catch training on the future.

checks.claim: No item scored in the frozen window was already interacted with in history.
The split lands on 60 / 20 / 20 of each learner's stream.
The trending signal is built from history events only.

groups.name: features
groups.purpose: The matrix handed to the ranker is finite, bounded, and carries signal.

checks.claim: The ranker never sees NaN or infinity.
Every feature stays inside [0, 1] before standardisation.
The fit set is not degenerate after negative sampling.
Each feature actually varies across the fit set.
checks.detail: A feature with almost no spread cannot separate classes no matter what coefficient it receives.

checks.claim: Every feature earns a non-trivial coefficient.
checks.detail: Inert features are kept because they are cheap and would matter on a catalog with real variance, but they are not doing work on this dataset.

groups.name: model
groups.purpose: The ranker is measured on data it did not fit, and its score is described honestly.

checks.claim: The ranker orders held-out examples better than chance.
checks.detail: Cross-validated inside the ranker-fit window; the frozen window is untouched.

checks.claim: The sigmoid output can be read as an engagement probability.
checks.detail: class_weight='balanced' reweights the classes, so the sigmoid output orders candidates but overstates absolute engagement probability. Use it for ordering, not for expected-value maths.

checks.claim: Per-item feature contributions sum back to the logit that produced the score.

groups.name: retrieval
groups.purpose: Candidate generation obeys the contracts the slate depends on.

checks.claim: The four retrieval routes rank the catalog differently.
checks.detail: Before trending was time-decayed this pair sat at 0.99, which made one route a duplicate of popularity.

checks.claim: Items already interacted with never reappear in a slate.
Each policy honours its own creator cap.
A request for 8 items returns 8 items.
Retrieval surfaces the frozen-window positives the ranker is asked to find.
checks.detail: NDCG@10 cannot exceed this ceiling. Ranking work is wasted on anything retrieval never proposes.

groups.name: evaluation
groups.purpose: Published metrics match a live recomputation.

checks.claim: Every published metric is inside its mathematically valid range.
The 95% interval brackets the mean it was resampled from.
The ranking gain over popularity is distinguishable from no gain.
checks.detail: 62 evaluable learners is a small sample; the interval is wide even when the point estimate is large.

checks.claim: The committed evaluation artifact is what this build actually produces.
checks.detail: Regenerate with: python -m signalweave.train, which rewrites it as part of registering.

checks.claim: Every policy the API can serve has frozen-window metrics of its own.
checks.detail: Otherwise the console would show one policy's slate next to another policy's numbers.

checks.claim: The promoted challenger outranks the best baseline, not just the weakest one.
checks.detail: The release gate compares against popularity only. Balanced trades ranking accuracy for slate diversity on purpose, so this gap is a product choice — but it is a gap, and the gate does not test for it.

checks.claim: The release status follows from the individual guardrails.
checks.expected: status is promote_to_shadow only when every guardrail passes
